rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP2PPP/R.notes: Called Bf4 the light-squared bishop and mentioned a later e3, but White's e-pawn has been exchanged. Rerouted the bishop 'via e3 to d2', which is not a plan.

r1b1kbnr/pppp1Npp/8/6q1/2BnP3/8/PPPP1PPP.notes: Described the position as if White were winning; after 5.Nxf7 Black has the famous mate. Suggested Qf3 or Ke2 as defences; neither is available as a defence here. Promised White 'the winning advantage' after surviving.

r1bq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/n2p1np1/6B1/2PPP3/2N5/.notes: Called the g5-bishop light-squared; it is the dark-squared one, and the trade comes via Bh6.

rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/3p4/3P1B2/8/PP2PPPP/R.notes: Called Bf4 the light-squared bishop. Gave a knight route Nc3-e2-g3 that no line uses.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/5P2/PPPPP1PP/RNB.notes: Suggested Nf3, but the f-pawn stands on f3. Called the c5/h4 targets light squares; 1.f3 weakens the dark squares.

rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3qp3/2B5/5P2/PPPP2P.notes: Praised 4...Qxd5 as seizing the initiative; it hangs the queen to 5.Bxd5. Called 5.Bxd5 Nxd5 'slightly passive but solid' for White.

r1bqk2r/p3p1bp/2p3pn/2Np4/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP.notes: Presented it as a White system and called c6/d5 doubled pawns. Gave ...Nf7 as a challenge to the c5-knight; from f7 it does not reach c5.

r1b1k2r/ppp2pbp/n2p2p1/3Pp3/2n1P2Q/2N2P2.notes: Said the queens were traded and that White has the bishop pair; Black gave the queen for both White bishops and two pawns. Had White using a bishop pair it no longer has.

rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/3PP3/2N5/PPP2PP.notes: Mentioned a semi-open c-file; Black's pawn still stands on c6.

rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/4pn2/8/2pP4/2N2NP1/PP2.notes: Gave Qa4+ with tempo; with Black castled it is not check.

rnbqkbnr/ppppp1pp/8/5p2/3P4/7P/PPP1PPP1/.notes: Paired the g4 plan with a g3 fianchetto, which contradicts it.

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/3PP3/3B4/PPP2PP.notes: Description says White develops "often at the cost of the d4-pawn" and Plan 2 says White "often sacrifices the d4-pawn after ...dxe4"; the brief (unsourced) gives 3...dxe4 4.Bxe4 Nf6 with an easy game for Black and no d4 gambit. Plan 1's f4-f5 attack is also unconfirmed. Needs a source on the 3.Bd3 lines before rewriting.

rnbqkb1r/1p2pppp/p4n2/3p4/3P4/2N2N2/PP2P.notes: Plan 1: The pawns are symmetrical (d4 against d5, c-file open), so there is no minority attack. Plan 2: Omitted ...Bf5 before ...e6; the brief has Black developing the light-squared bishop before locking it in.

r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2nb1n2/3pp3/P7/1PP1P1P1.notes: Plan 1: White's d-pawn is still on d2.

rnbqkbnr/pppppp1p/8/6p1/5PP1/8/PPPPP2P/R.notes: Plan 2: White's pawn is still on g4, so the g-file is half-open for Black, not open.

r1bq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/2n2np1/8/2QPP3/2N2N2/P.notes: Plan 2: ...Na5 attacks the queen on c4, not d4; ...Bg4 pins the f3-knight that defends d4.

rnbqkb1r/pppp1p1p/5n2/6N1/4PppP/8/PPPP2P.notes: Plan 3: e4 holds White's own pawn and f3 is covered by Black's g4-pawn, so the knight cannot go to either square.

rnbqkbnr/pppp2pp/8/5p2/4Pp2/5N2/PPPP2PP/.notes: Plan 2: ...Qh4+ hangs the queen to Nxh4; the f3-knight covers h4.

r1bq1rk1/pppn1pbp/3p1np1/3Pp1B1/2P1P3/2N.notes: Plan 2: ...Qe8 and ...Ne8 need the same square; the knight goes to h7 after ...h6. Plan 4: ...a5 secures c5 (for ...Nd7-c5), not b6.

rnbqk2r/ppp1ppb1/3p1npp/6B1/2PP4/2N2N2/P.notes: Description: The c1-bishop on g5 is dark-squared.

r1bqkbnr/2pp1ppp/p1n5/1p2p3/4P3/1B3N2/PP.notes: Plan 1: The g1-knight is already on f3; the Spanish manoeuvre is Nb1-d2-f1-g3. Plan 2: Neither side has a queenside majority (a6, b5, c7 against a2, b2, c2).

rnb1k2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/5q2/1b1P4/1QN2N2/PP.notes: Plan 4: Exchanging on c3 after a3 gives the bishop pair to White, not Black.

rnbqkb1r/p2ppppp/5n2/1ppP2B1/8/5N2/PPP1P.notes: Description: Black's e7-pawn blocks the g5-d8 diagonal, so the f6-knight is not pinned. Plan 2: There is no pin (e7-pawn in the way).

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp1p/3p1np1/8/3PP3/8/PPPN1P.notes: Description: Nbd2 does nothing against ...Bg4, which pins nothing while the e2-pawn stands; the point of the move is to keep c3 free. Plan 4: A knight on c5 is attacked by the d4-pawn, and from c5 it would not hit d4 anyway.

rnb1k1nr/pp2ppbp/3p2p1/q1pP4/2P1P3/2N5/P.notes: Plan 3: Qc2 defends the knight but leaves it pinned to the king; only interposing on d2 breaks the pin.

r1bqkb1r/pppnpppp/5n2/8/Q1pP4/5N2/PP2PPP.notes: Description: 4.Qa4+ is about regaining c4; it does not prevent ...c5.

rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/1bPP4/2N5/PP2PP.notes: Plan 4: cxd5 exd5 gives a Carlsbad structure with Black's c7-pawn intact, not an isolated d-pawn or hanging pawns.

rnb2rk1/p1p1qpp1/1p5p/3p4/3P4/4PN2/PP2BP.notes: Description: Black's c7-pawn is still on the board, so the c-file is half-open for White. Plan 2: Black has one light-squared bishop, and three queenside pawns against White's two, so there is no Black minority attack.

rnb1kbnr/pp2pppp/1qp5/3p4/3P1B2/5N2/PPP1.notes: Plan 1: Ra2 is impossible with White's pawn on a2. Plan 3: A light-squared bishop on f5 cannot challenge the dark-squared Bf4; ...Bd6 can.
